title: Tiger Rag and the flood-damaged Kimball piano
summary: Black Benny's hat-box trick, then Broussard explains his waterlogged piano and the numbers and seven or eight styles he could play.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: He had a big round hat box with a cord rising and he pull it and say, hold that tiger. Ooh, hold that tiger. Ooh, hold that tiger. And he'd be pulling and playing all the time. Yeah, and he'd pull it and he'd play. And the tiger rag was a famous rag at that time, the tiger rag. And I used to play all them kind of, all them kind of numbers. Of course, I mean, you know, uh, if I'd have had any time, uh, I mean, I mean, I, I'd run over them and I'd play those numbers. I still have them in mind and when they're in your mind, you can, it don't take no more than a short time to come in. But those kind of numbers, the piano has to be in fair shape. Now, uh, uh, this, this piano, as I said before, it's all damp. It's in, it's pretty good piano. Uh, it has to be for the stoutness water. It's been underwater, halfway underwater, you know, uh, for at least, uh, two weeks. You see, it had to be. It's a Kimball. And, uh, now if I had some care, if I had got the kerosene, I'd have painted with oil and that kind of stuff. Then it would have had, action would have been there and I could have played some of those good numbers. I could have played like the Messwright Ramble and the Tiger Rag and, and, uh, some of the numbers that I was really, the diplomat blues, see, and them kind of numbers. Uh, they, they were good numbers and you could really get away with them. That's what really showed your skill in the piano. But, uh, I can't get away, get away with it, you know. No, no, no, no, no. I can't get away with it.
I'm surprised you do so wonderful things you do on that piano.

Yeah, and those beats, there was such wonderful beats. Like, see them, the diplomat blues when they come in? Mm-hm. You can't get away with it. It makes you stumble over the notes. But I'll tell you, as soon as I'm able to get this thing in shape, which it don't take too much to put it back in shape, just a little kerosene and be on it for a few hours and a couple of good dry days. And then I'm going to have the, if y'all get a chance to come back again. And then I could really play some of those numbers as they supposedly, because I got a different style. See, I didn't play all the styles that I played. I played about seven or eight different styles of piano. See, I had to do that when it'd make it warm for me. I'd get out one note and get another, see, because I'd maybe be playing in one note and those guys been out there listening. See, and they'd come on in and they'd pick
up on that. Excuse me. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And it almost swept the neighborhood away. Yeah. Sure.
